methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Column: For rural Virginia, data centers are more than technology - The Virginian-Pilot
signals.signal_reading: A $50M+ AI data center infrastructure investment in Henrico with 200 jobs signals deepening technical capacity concentration in Richmond Metro, creating middle-skill opportunities but requiring specialized expertise that may not distribute beyond the metro corridor.

signals.title: Prince William Co. supervisors deny 2,000-acre Dulles South data center plans
signals.signal_reading: Prince William County's rejection of 2,000-acre data center plans suggests political resistance to infrastructure expansion even in NoVA, potentially constraining the physical foundation for distributed AI capability while concentrating it further in existing Loudoun/Fairfax sites.

signals.title: Virginia's best-paying jobs are most exposed to AI, report says - Axios
signals.signal_reading: Report showing Virginia's highest-paying jobs face greatest AI exposure reveals a concentration risk: metro knowledge workers have resources to adapt while rural workers in lower-paying roles lack access to AI upskilling, accelerating the capability divide.

signals.title: Mountain Empire Community College closing workforce center, relocating programs to campus
signals.signal_reading: Mountain Empire Community College closing its workforce center during AI transition consolidates training capacity on main campus, reducing distributed access points precisely when Southwest Virginia needs expanded tech workforce development infrastructure.

signals.title: To defend your software, first teach AI to break it - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Tech research teaching AI to break software demonstrates deep technical capability development in New River Valley that could distribute through the university system's extension network, though currently concentrated in academic research settings.
